Sir/Madam,

As part of the annual renewal process for the above-mentioned shelter, an inspection of the premises was conducted on 20.04.2024 by the undersigned along with the Sanitary Inspector and the Social Welfare Officer (Zone I). The purpose of the inspection was to verify compliance with the conditions of registration and to assess the general condition of the shelter, its facilities, and the welfare of its residents.

The following is the report of the inspection:

1. General Information

Name of Shelter: Asha Kiran Shelter
Registration No.: MHA-2023-0561
Registered Manager: Smt. Kamla Verma (as per records)
Address of Shelter: House No. 89, Gandhi Road, Mumbai – 400012
Date of Inspection: 20.04.2024
Time of Inspection: 10:30 AM to 1:15 PM

2. Team Present

1. Shri R. P. Jadhav, Assistant Municipal Commissioner (Social Welfare) – Inspecting Officer
2. Smt. P. N. Kulkarni, Sanitary Inspector
3. Shri V. B. Patil, Social Welfare Officer (Zone I)
4. Shri Mahesh Devi, Caretaker (representing the shelter management)

Note: The registered manager, Smt. Kamla Verma, was not present at the time of inspection. The caretaker, Shri Mahesh Devi, stated that she was on leave due to ill health and that he was authorised to assist the inspection team.

3. Observations and Findings

3.1 Premises and Infrastructure

The shelter is located in a two-storey building. The ground floor comprises the reception area, office, kitchen, dining hall, and two dormitories. The first floor has three dormitories, a store room, and a medical room. The building appears to be in a satisfactory structural condition, with no visible signs of dampness, leakage, or disrepair.

The dormitories are clean and well-ventilated. However, it was observed that the floor space per resident in Dorm B on the ground floor is approximately 28 square feet, which is marginally below the prescribed minimum of 30 square feet per person. The management was advised to reduce the occupancy of this dormitory or to reconfigure the space to meet the standard.

3.2 Sanitation and Hygiene

The toilets and bathrooms were found to be clean and adequately maintained. There are four toilets and four bathrooms for women and three toilets and three bathrooms for men. The Sanitary Inspector noted that the drainage system in the men's toilet block was slightly clogged and requires immediate attention. A recommendation has been made to rectify this within one week.

3.3 Kitchen and Food

The kitchen was found to be hygienic, with adequate storage for dry rations. The menu for the week was displayed on the notice board. The residents confirmed that they receive two meals per day, along with tea in the morning. The food was being prepared at the time of inspection and appeared to be of good quality and quantity.

3.4 Medical Facilities

A medical room is available on the first floor, and a visiting doctor attends the shelter every Tuesday and Friday. The medical register was checked and found to be up to date. A stock of basic medicines was available in the medical room.

However, it was observed that the floor space per resident in Dorm B on the ground floor is approximately 28 square feet, which is marginally below the prescribed minimum of 30 square feet per person. The management was advised to reduce the occupancy of this dormitory or to reconfigure the space to meet the standard.

3.2 Sanitation and Hygiene

The toilets and bathrooms were found to be clean and adequately maintained. There are four toilets and four bathrooms for women and three toilets and three bathrooms for men. The Sanitary Inspector noted that the drainage system in the men's toilet block was slightly clogged and requires immediate attention. A recommendation has been made to rectify this within one week.

3.3 Kitchen and Food

The kitchen was found to be hygienic, with adequate storage for dry rations. The menu for the week was displayed on the notice board. The residents confirmed that they receive two meals per day, along with tea in the morning. The food was being prepared at the time of inspection and appeared to be of good quality and quantity.

3.4 Medical Facilities

A medical room is available on the first floor, and a visiting doctor attends the shelter every Tuesday and Friday. The medical register was checked and found to be up to date. A stock of basic medicines was available in the medical room.

**SECTION A: FAMILY BACKGROUND**

Resident said her father died when she was a child and her mother died about five years ago. She said she has two brothers, both older, who are married and live in the same village. She said she does not have a good relationship with her brothers and they do not help her. She said one brother works in Cuttack as a mason and the other is a farmer. She said her brothers did not support her when she left her husband.

Resident said she is married for about 15 years. She said she has two daughters, aged 13 and 9. She said both daughters are living with her husband at her in-laws' house in Badapokhari. She said she was not allowed to take her daughters with her. Resident became emotional when speaking about her daughters. She said she misses them and wants to see them.

Resident said her husband is a daily wage labourer. She said he drinks alcohol regularly and becomes violent. She said her in-laws also used to scold her and sometimes beat her. She said her mother-in-law died two years ago and her father-in-law is old and stays at home.

**SECTION B: REASON FOR SEEKING SHELTER**

Resident said her husband has been beating her for many years. She said the beatings increased after he started drinking more about three years ago. She said he also used to take her earnings and spend them on alcohol. She said she tried to tolerate the situation for the sake of her daughters.

Resident said on 8 August 2024 her husband came home drunk and beat her badly because she had gone to her neighbour's house without his permission. She said he also broke a cooking pot and threw her clothes outside. She said she was scared and went to her brother's house in the same village, but her brother's wife told her to go back to her husband. Resident said she then went to the village panchayat office on 9 August. The panchayat samiti member advised her to go to the CDPO office. The CDPO office gave her a referral letter and arranged transport to the shelter.

**B1. Any previous shelter stay:** No
**B2. Previous complaints filed (police / other):** No police complaint. Panchayat mediation was attempted once in July 2024 but did not lead to any change.
**B3. Willingness to pursue legal action:** Resident said she is willing to consider legal action but is worried about her daughters. She said she wants to be able to see her daughters regularly.
